=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/security_audit.sh | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[4]
  Line or code reference: security_audit_emit_path_diagnostic at lines 65-80 (round 4 hunk), specifically the `LC_ALL=C tr -d '\000\r' 2>/dev/null < "${diagnostic_file}" | LC_ALL=C grep -E '…' | LC_ALL=C grep -vxF -f "${diagnostic_prompt_file}" | tail -n 20` chain; the same shape also lives in `security_audit_emit_codex_stderr_tail` at lines 215-220 (round 1 hunk) where stderr is normalised with `tr -d '\000\r'` before `grep -vxF -f "${stderr_prompt_file}"`.
  PROBLEM: The stderr stream is normalised with `tr -d '\000\r'` so echoed lines lose any carriage returns, but the rendered-prompt file (`${diagnostic_prompt_file}` / `${stderr_prompt_file}`) is passed to `grep -vxF -f` verbatim. When the project-spec content is appended to the prompt in findings-json mode (the agent explicitly noted that project spec is "appended verbatim to the prompt"), a CRLF-formatted spec keeps `\r` at the end of every line in the prompt file, while the Codex stderr echo of that same line is LF-only. The exact-line filter therefore fails to drop the echoed line, and a spec line that happens to contain "No such file or directory", "os error 2", or "ENOENT" leaks through `captured_path_error=` and through the masked tail's prompt filter, violating the documented "Lines that echo the rendered prompt are dropped." invariant (PR description checklist item 5; agents.md note; changelog fragment).
  WHY: `codex exec` writes its stderr as LF-only, so the echo of a CRLF prompt line will not carry the trailing `\r` that the prompt file retains. `grep -vxF` compares the entire line byte-for-byte; a single `\r` mismatch makes the filter return the line. The round-4 regression test writes the spec with `"\n"` (`spec_path.write_text(spec_line + "\n", encoding="utf-8")`), so it never exercises the CRLF path that the agent identified in pass 1 (cross-pollination finding from openai/gpt-6-luna, severity=high, confidence=[4], pointing at the same `LC_ALL=C tr -d '\000\r' < "${diagnostic_file}" | … grep -vxF -f "${diagnostic_prompt_file}"` chain). The same fix has to be applied to `security_audit_emit_codex_stderr_tail`, which has the identical asymmetry.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- scripts/security_audit.sh | severity=NIT | confidence=[3]
  Line or code reference: 80-82 (path diagnostic) and 219-221 (tail helper)
  PROBLEM: The prompt-echo filter strips carriage returns from stderr but not from the rendered prompt file, so a CRLF-formatted project spec can evade the filter.
  WHY: At line 374, the project spec is appended verbatim to the rendered prompt via `cat`. If the spec has CRLF line endings (common on Windows), the prompt file retains `\r`. At line 80, stderr has `\r` stripped via `tr -d '\000\r'`. At line 82, `grep -vxF -f "${diagnostic_prompt_file}"` compares the stripped stderr lines against prompt lines that still have `\r`. They don't match, so an echoed project-spec line containing a path-error phrase is not filtered and reaches `captured_path_error=`. The same issue exists in the tail helper at lines 219-221. The regression test at `test_security_audit_codex_path_diagnostic_drops_prompt_echo_lines` uses an LF-formatted spec, so it does not cover this case. The masks still apply, so this is defense-in-depth rather than a secret leak, but the code inconsistency (stripping `\r` from one side but not the other) is real.
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
- scripts/security_audit.sh | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[4]
  Line or code reference: lines 80-83, security_audit_emit_path_diagnostic — the prompt-echo filter added in review round 4
  PROBLEM: The diagnostic normalizes stderr with `tr -d '\000\r'` (line 80) before exact-line filtering, but does not normalize the rendered prompt file (line 82, `grep -vxF -f "${diagnostic_prompt_file}"`). When the project spec has CRLF line endings, the rendered prompt file (built at line 374 via `cat "${SECURITY_AUDIT_PROJECT_SPEC_PATH}"`) retains CR characters in those lines. On Linux with LC_ALL=C, `grep` treats CR as a regular character, so the prompt pattern `Spec note: ...\r` never matches the CR-stripped stderr line `Spec note: ...`. The echoed spec line is therefore not dropped and appears in `captured_path_error=`, violating the documented prompt-echo exclusion invariant. The same asymmetry exists pre-existing in the tail function (lines 219-221), but the last run replicates it in the new path-diagnostic code path.
  WHY: A CRLF-formatted project spec whose content includes "No such file or directory", "os error 2", or "ENOENT" is echoed by `codex exec` to stderr. The path diagnostic selects it via `grep -E`, strips CR from it via `tr -d '\000\r'`, then fails to match it against the CR-bearing prompt line via `grep -vxF -f`. The spec line is printed as `captured_path_error=` before the tail's prompt filter also fails to drop it. The regression test `test_security_audit_codex_path_diagnostic_drops_prompt_echo_lines` uses LF-formatted spec content, so it does not exercise this path.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
